audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Hwei's key ability "Subject: Fear (CC Paints)" in eleven separate fields. No such ability exists.
audit.why: Hwei's E is Subject: Torment — the palette that holds Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw, i.e. all of his crowd control. It is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10. Q is Subject: Disaster (10/9/8/7/6), W is Subject: Serenity (18/17.5/17/16.5/16), R is Spiraling Despair (120/100/80). The packet flags that the matchup never names a single real Hwei ability.
audit.corrected: Every occurrence of the fabricated name replaced with Subject: Torment, and breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt on the real per-rank numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer read "Skill" on rows 0 and 3 where the content layer and packet levelChart read Orianna and Hwei.
audit.why: At level 1 Hwei must load a two-part paint before anything resolves while Command: Attack is instant, so Orianna leads. At 4-5 Subject: Torment zones her off the wave and Subject: Disaster pokes from beyond her 815 Q.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side -> Orianna, phases[3].side -> Hwei, with both whys rewritten to match.

audit.why: The content spike text is unusually specific for this repo — it already tracks the palette combos and the two-item flip to instant Shockwave over telegraphed painters. Nothing to correct.

notes: The headline defect here is a fabricated ability: the full layer called Hwei's key ability 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' in eleven fields. The real E is Subject: Torment, which is what actually holds all of his crowd control. Every occurrence is replaced. The four report edits all exist solely to remove that fabricated name. Chart disagreed on rows 0 and 3 only; full layer moved onto the content values, which match packet.levelChart, so no win[N] edits were needed. The content layer is notably better written than the full layer on this matchup and needed almost nothing.
